_comment: Semantic fingerprints for the strict-static acceptance tracks, used by
scripts/gs.ps1 to decide whether a change regressed anything.
Every field here except trace_events is architectural state and must not
move. trace_events legitimately changes when interior resume aliases are
added, so it is recorded for reference but never gates.
A FULLY_STATIC headline alone does NOT establish 'no regression' - these
invariants are what does. See docs/GS011_TRANSIENT_IMAGES.md,
'Verifying no regression properly'.
Measured 2026-08-07 on a non-LTO build (141,778,857 bytes), after the
recompiler learned to resume into a THUMB BL_suffix (717 entries) and
after seeding Func_2df0 and the RAM-space Func_8d4.
Both 5,400-frame tracks AND the 21,600-frame campaign track are now
FULLY_STATIC. Coverage is frame-bounded and track-bounded: 'campaign' is
ONE deterministic route, and another route will find its own gaps.
trace_events fell ~303k on both 5,400-frame tracks in this revision while
every semantic invariant stayed byte-identical. The likely cause is the
Func_8d4 resume alias: it sits in the constantly-running boot/IRQ IWRAM
block, so the runtime resumes inline instead of emitting a dispatch record
each time. That is a PLAUSIBLE mechanism, not a verified one - it has not
been confirmed, and it is recorded here so the drop is not mistaken for a
regression or waved through as noise.

_status: RETIRED as a gate, deliberately - not deleted, so nobody re-adds it
assuming it was forgotten. The 21,600-frame campaign track below is the
same deterministic route run longer, so it strictly supersedes this one.
Its last measured figures were cycles=1897809555 steps=39917

trace_events demonstrably moved on every other track in that revision.
Re-measure before ever trusting these numbers again.

This was NOT accepted as noise. It was bisected: a 10,800-frame run of
the same route after the change is BIT-IDENTICAL to the baseline
measured before any of it (cycles=1897809555 steps=39917
ppu_vcount=171). So nothing changed through 10,800 frames; the ~1%
cycle drift appears only between 10,800 and 21,600. Final visual state
is unchanged (pal 959/1024, vram 59741/98304, oam 535/1024) and the
track is still FULLY_STATIC with zero misses.
OPEN QUESTION, not resolved: the likely mechanism is that seeding
changed host function partitioning, and IRQ recognition happens at host
function boundaries rather than at every guest instruction as real
hardware does. If that is right, emulated interrupt timing is sensitive
to how we partition translations - which would matter for audio and
timing-sensitive effects, and is related to the still-open GS-010
DISPSTAT cycle-drift item. This has NOT been confirmed; it is written
down so the next person starts from the evidence rather than from the
assumption that a re-baseline meant nothing happened.
